what: Plan 68 step 0 (the gate, 3a) and the desk test (3b): how long a chat summary takes on the Deck's own AI server, and what it writes.
how: Script on the PC (session scratchpad gate.py) talking to the Deck's Ollama 0.34.1 over an SSH tunnel. Model gemma4:e2b-it-qat, num_ctx 16384, think false, num_predict 400, temperature 0.3, keep_alive 240m (the Deck's own). Input = the chat's turns in the chat memory's own line format (question <=200 chars, answer <=400, bonsai fences stripped with chat_memory_service.strip_fenced_blocks, 'Request cancelled.' skipped), everything except the newest 4 turns. A random 'Notes request NNNN.' first line and rotating wording defeat the server's saved reading between runs.

chats.d2aa6252: 'wheatley fight', 144 turns, mixed games (mostly none recorded; Half-Life 2, Hades, Hollow Knight, Black Mesa), 2 hidden spoiler blocks (one Hollow Knight)
chats.351b2838: 'parrying', 66 turns, Deep Rock Galactic: Survivor, no hidden blocks

conditions.game / cold-game: Half-Life 2 at its main menu (60 fps, GPU ~19%)
conditions.level / cold-level / level-v2 / level-v3: Half-Life 2 in a loaded save (Route Kanal), 60 fps
conditions.cold-*: model unloaded before each run (keep_alive 0, confirmed gone from /api/ps)

wordings.v2: added 'one fact per line, no headings and no bold' -> listed every question, hit the 400 cap on the long chat (47.0 s)
wordings.v3 (chosen): 'at most 10 short plain lines ... Group similar questions into one line. Newer topics matter more ... Leave out the helper's own tone of voice. No headings, no bold.'

verdict.gate: PASS. Worst with a game running and the chosen wording: 39.6 s (cold start, in a level, the 144-turn chat). Worst of every run with a game: 47.0 s (v2 wording, which is not used). Nothing reached a minute.
verdict.time_limit: 120 s = 3 x 39.6 s rounded (plan 68 section 8 question 2 default: 3 x worst with a game, never under 60).
verdict.input_cap: 9,000 tokens: the 144-turn chat is ~8,650 tokens and read in 26.6 s during play; a bigger input would push a cold start past a minute.
verdict.Q1_quality: v3 names the games and groups what was asked in 50-85 words; v1 described the character voice as if the player asked for it, fixed in v3.
verdict.Q2_hidden_notes: No hidden-note text in any summary. One automatic flag ('dodging', cold-level v1) is a false alarm: the visible answers say 'dodge that stuff' and 'dash patterns'.
verdict.Q3_follow_up: Not run at the desk; answered by SUMUP-01 and CHAT-MEMORY-01 on the device after the build.
verdict.Q4_language: Spanish reply language -> the summary came back in Spanish (level-v2-es).
verdict.next_answer_start: A summary does not slow the next answer's start: an answer-shaped 2,814-token front re-read in 0.43-0.51 s both before and right after each summary (the server kept its saved reading).
